title: Handle fragmented QUIC ClientHello in next_layer
answers: Why does mitmproxy fail to read SNI or match ignore-hosts on fragmented QUIC ClientHellos?
How should next_layer handle incomplete QUIC datagrams during ClientHello parsing?
Why are QUIC connections with large ClientHellos not matching allow-hosts or ignore-hosts?
body:
Symptom: Connections using QUIC fail to match --ignore-hosts or --allow-hosts rules when the ClientHello is fragmented across packets.
Root cause: mitmproxy/addons/next_layer.py:_get_client_hello treats quic_parse_client_hello_from_datagrams returning None as absence of a ClientHello instead of an incomplete datagram.
Fix pattern: In the UDP/QUIC handler, check if the parsed ClientHello is None and raise NeedsMoreData so the connection waits for additional datagram fragments.
Constraints: Applies to protocols and parsers that return None on incomplete datagrams; invalid datagrams raising ValueError must still be caught and ignored.
says: Traffic ignore rules fail to match encrypted connections with large initial packet handshakes.
Connections using modern fast UDP protocols bypass host filter lists when packets fragment.
Domain filtering rules ignore connections when initial handshake data is split across packets.
Ensure host exclusion filters properly inspect fragmented initial connection packets from modern clients.
